paras.en: He was in the region of asteroids 325, 326, 327, 328, 329 and 330. So he began by visiting them to find something to do and to learn.
paras.zh: 他当时在325、326、327、328、329和330号小行星所在的区域。于是，他先去一一拜访，想找点事情做，也长些见识。

paras.en: The first was inhabited by a king. Dressed in purple and ermine, the king sat on a throne that was very simple yet majestic.
paras.zh: 第一颗小行星上住着一位国王。国王身穿紫袍，披着白鼬皮斗篷，坐在一张十分简朴却又庄严的宝座上。

paras.en: “Ah! Here is a subject!” cried the king when he caught sight of the little prince.
paras.zh: “啊！来了一个臣民！”国王一看见小王子，就叫了起来。

paras.en: And the little prince wondered:
paras.zh: 小王子便在心里纳闷：

paras.en: “How can he recognise me when he has never seen me before!”
paras.zh: “他从来没见过我，怎么会认出我呢！”

paras.en: He did not know that, for kings, the world is made very simple. All people are subjects.
paras.zh: 他不知道，对国王们来说，世界被简化得很厉害。所有人都是臣民。

paras.en: “Come closer so I can see you better,” said the king, who was so proud to be someone's king at last.
paras.zh: “走近些，让我看清楚你。”国王对他说。他终于成了某个人的国王，心里得意极了。

paras.en: The little prince looked around for somewhere to sit, but the magnificent ermine cloak took up the whole planet. So he stayed standing, and as he was tired, he yawned.
paras.zh: 小王子四下寻找可以坐的地方，可那件华美的白鼬皮斗篷把整个星球都占满了。他只好继续站着，因为累了，便打了个哈欠。

paras.en: “It is against etiquette to yawn in the presence of a king,” the monarch told him. “I forbid you to do so.”
paras.zh: “在国王面前打哈欠，是不合礼仪的。”这位君主对他说，“我不准你这样做。”

paras.en: “I can't help it,” replied the little prince, quite embarrassed. “I've had a long journey and I haven't slept...”
paras.zh: “我忍不住呀。”小王子很不好意思地回答，“我经过了漫长的旅行，一直没睡过觉……”

paras.en: “Then,” the king told him, “I order you to yawn. I haven’t seen anyone yawn for years. Yawns are curiosities to me. Come on! Yawn again. That’s an order.”
paras.zh: “那么，”国王对他说，“我命令你打哈欠。我已经好多年没见过谁打哈欠了。打哈欠对我来说是件稀奇事。来吧！再打一个哈欠。这是命令。”

paras.en: “That makes me nervous… I can’t any more…” said the little prince, blushing deeply.
paras.zh: “这样我会紧张……我打不出来了……”小王子说，脸涨得通红。

paras.en: “Hmm! Hmm!” replied the king. “Then I… I order you sometimes to yawn and sometimes to…”
paras.zh: “嗯！嗯！”国王回答，“那么我……我命令你一会儿打哈欠，一会儿……”

paras.en: He stumbled over his words a little and seemed annoyed.
paras.zh: 他说话有点结巴，看上去有些恼火。

paras.en: For what mattered most to the king was that his authority should be respected. He would not tolerate disobedience. He was an absolute monarch. But since he was very kind, he gave reasonable orders.
paras.zh: 因为国王最在意的，就是自己的权威得到尊重。他容不得别人不服从。他是一位拥有绝对权力的君主。不过，他心地很好，所以他下的命令都合情合理。

paras.en: “If I ordered,” he often said, “if I ordered a general to turn into a seabird, and if the general did not obey, it would not be the general’s fault. It would be my fault.”
paras.zh: “如果我命令，”他常常说，“如果我命令一位将军变成一只海鸟，而如果将军没有服从，那就不是将军的错。那是我的错。”

paras.en: “May I sit down?” the little prince asked shyly.
paras.zh: “我可以坐下吗？”小王子怯生生地问。

paras.en: “I order you to sit down,” replied the king, majestically drawing back part of his ermine cloak.
paras.zh: “我命令你坐下。”国王回答他，同时威严地收起白鼬皮披风的一角。

paras.en: But the little prince was puzzled. The planet was tiny. What could the king possibly rule over?
paras.zh: 可是小王子很纳闷。这颗星球小极了。国王究竟能统治些什么呢？

paras.en: “Your Majesty…” he said to him. “Please forgive me for asking you questions…”
paras.zh: “陛下……”他对国王说，“请原谅我向您提问……”

paras.en: “I order you to ask me questions,” the king said hastily.
paras.zh: “我命令你向我提问。”国王赶忙说。

paras.en: “Your Majesty... what do you rule over?”
paras.zh: “陛下……您统治着什么呢？”

paras.en: “Over everything,” the king replied, very simply.
paras.zh: “一切。”国王十分自然地回答。

paras.en: “Over everything?”
paras.zh: “一切？”

paras.en: With a slight gesture, the king pointed to his planet, the other planets and the stars.
paras.zh: 国王轻轻做了个手势，指向自己的星球、其他星球，还有星星。

paras.en: “Over all that?” said the little prince.
paras.zh: “这一切都归您统治？”小王子说。

paras.en: “Over all that...” replied the king.
paras.zh: “这一切都归我统治……”国王回答。

paras.en: For he was not only an absolute monarch, but a universal monarch.
paras.zh: 因为他不只是拥有绝对权力的君主，还是统治整个宇宙的君主。

paras.en: “And do the stars obey you?”
paras.zh: “那么，星星也服从您吗？”

paras.en: “Of course,” the king told him. “They obey at once. I do not tolerate a lack of discipline.”
paras.zh: “当然，”国王对他说，“它们立刻就服从。我不能容忍不守纪律。”

paras.en: Such power filled the little prince with wonder. If he had possessed it himself, he could have watched not forty-four, but seventy-two, or even a hundred, or even two hundred sunsets in a single day, without ever having to pull his chair along! And as the memory of his little planet, which he had left behind, made him a little sad, he found the courage to ask the king for a favour:
paras.zh: 这样的权力让小王子惊叹不已。如果他自己也拥有这样的权力，就能在同一天里看到日落，不是四十四次，而是七十二次，甚至一百次，甚至两百次，一次也不用拖动椅子！想到自己离开后留下的那颗小星球，他有些难过，于是鼓起勇气，请国王赐他一份恩惠：

paras.en: “I would like to see a sunset… Please do this for me… Order the sun to set…”
paras.zh: “我想看一次日落……请让我高兴一下吧……命令太阳落下去吧……”

paras.en: “If I ordered a general to fly from flower to flower like a butterfly, or to write a tragedy, or to turn into a seabird, and if the general did not carry out the order he had been given, which of us would be in the wrong—him or me?”
paras.zh: “如果我命令一位将军像蝴蝶那样，从一朵花飞到另一朵花上，或者写一出悲剧，或者变成一只海鸟，而这位将军没有执行收到的命令，那么，是他错了，还是我错了？”

paras.en: “You would,” said the little prince firmly.
paras.zh: “是您错了。”小王子坚定地说。

paras.en: “Exactly. You must demand of each person what each person can give,” the king went on. “Authority rests first of all on reason. If you order your people to go and throw themselves into the sea, they will start a revolution. I have the right to demand obedience because my orders are reasonable.”
paras.zh: “没错。要求每个人做的，必须是每个人做得到的事，”国王接着说，“权威首先要以道理为基础。如果你命令你的人民去跳海，他们就会起来革命。我有权要求服从，因为我的命令是合理的。”

paras.en: “What about my sunset, then?” the little prince reminded him, for he never forgot a question once he had asked it.
paras.zh: “那我的日落呢？”小王子提醒他。他一旦提出一个问题，就从来不会忘记。

paras.en: “Your sunset—you will have it. I will demand it. But with my knowledge of government, I will wait until the conditions are favourable.”
paras.zh: “你的日落，你会看到的。我会下令的。不过，凭我治国的学问，我要等到条件有利的时候。”

paras.en: “When will that be?” asked the little prince.
paras.zh: “那是什么时候呢？”小王子问。

paras.en: “Ahem! Ahem!” replied the king, first consulting a thick calendar. “Ahem! Ahem! It will be about… about… it will be this evening at about seven forty! And you will see how well I am obeyed.”
paras.zh: “咳！咳！”国王先查了一本厚厚的日历，回答他，“咳！咳！大约在……大约在……就在今天晚上七点四十分左右！到时候你就会看到，我的命令执行得有多好。”

paras.en: The little prince yawned. He was sorry to have missed his sunset. And besides, he was already a little bored:
paras.zh: 小王子打了个哈欠。他为没看成那次日落而遗憾。而且，他已经有点无聊了：

paras.en: “I have nothing left to do here,” he said to the king. “I’m setting off again!”
paras.zh: “我在这里已经没什么可做的了，”他对国王说，“我要重新出发了！”

paras.en: “Don’t leave,” replied the king, who was so proud to have a subject. “Don’t leave. I’ll make you a minister!”
paras.zh: “别走，”国王回答，他为自己有了一个臣民而十分自豪，“别走，我让你当大臣！”

paras.en: “Minister of what?”
paras.zh: “管什么的大臣？”

paras.en: “Of… of justice!”
paras.zh: “管……管司法的！”

paras.en: “But there’s no one to judge!”
paras.zh: “可是，这里没有人可以审判呀！”

paras.en: “You never know,” the king told him. “I haven’t been all round my kingdom yet. I’m very old, I have no room for a carriage, and walking makes me tired.”
paras.zh: “这可说不准，”国王对他说，“我还没把我的王国走遍呢。我年纪很大了，这里又没地方放马车，走路也让我累。”

paras.en: “Oh! But I’ve already looked,” said the little prince, leaning over to take another look at the other side of the planet. “There’s no one over there either…”
paras.zh: “哦！可是我已经看过了，”小王子说着，探过身去，又朝星球的另一边看了一眼，“那边也没有人……”

paras.en: “Then you will judge yourself,” the king replied. “That is the hardest thing of all. It is much harder to judge yourself than to judge others. If you manage to judge yourself well, that means you are truly wise.”
paras.zh: “那你就审判你自己吧，”国王回答他，“这是最难的。审判自己比审判别人难得多。如果你能好好地审判自己，就说明你是一个真正有智慧的人。”

paras.en: “As for me,” said the little prince, “I can judge myself anywhere. I don’t need to live here.”
paras.zh: “我嘛，”小王子说，“我在哪里都可以审判自己，不必住在这里。”

paras.en: “Ahem! Ahem!” said the king. “I do believe there is an old rat somewhere on my planet. I hear him at night. You can judge this old rat. You will sentence him to death from time to time. That way, his life will depend on your justice. But you will pardon him every time, to avoid waste. There is only one.”
paras.zh: “咳！咳！”国王说，“我相信，我的星球上有个地方住着一只老老鼠。夜里我能听见它的声音。你可以审判这只老老鼠。你要时不时判它死刑。这样，它的性命就由你的司法来决定了。不过，为了节省，你每次都要赦免它。老鼠只有这么一只。”

paras.en: “As for me,” replied the little prince, “I don’t like sentencing anyone to death, and I really think I’ll be going.”
paras.zh: “我嘛，”小王子回答，“我不喜欢判死刑，我想我还是走吧。”

paras.en: “No,” said the king.
paras.zh: “不行。”国王说。

paras.en: But the little prince, having finished his preparations, did not want to hurt the old monarch’s feelings:
paras.zh: 可是，小王子已经做好了出发的准备，又不愿让这位年老的君主伤心：

paras.en: “If Your Majesty wished to be obeyed promptly, you could give me a reasonable order. You could order me, for example, to leave before a minute has passed. It seems to me that the conditions are favourable…”
paras.zh: “陛下，如果您希望命令得到及时的服从，就可以给我下一个合理的命令。比如，您可以命令我在一分钟之内离开。我觉得条件很有利……”

paras.en: The king gave no reply. The little prince hesitated at first, then, with a sigh, set off.
paras.zh: 国王什么也没回答，小王子先是犹豫了一下，然后叹了口气，便出发了。

paras.en: “I appoint you my ambassador,” the king then hastily called out.
paras.zh: “我任命你为我的大使。”国王这时赶忙喊道。

paras.en: He had a grand air of authority.
paras.zh: 他一副十分威严的样子。

paras.en: “Grown-ups are very strange,” the little prince said to himself as he travelled.
paras.zh: “大人们真奇怪，”小王子在旅途中暗自想。
